To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the steady streaming generated in an oscillatory flow in a pipe is affected by the shape and the length of the pipe, and that the steady streaming can be of a much larger order of magnitude if the ends of the oscillatory flow have different mean radii.

the first-order steady streaming induced in a pipe of varying cross-section by a purely oscillatory axial pressure difference is of order (ε 2 ) when the thickness of the Stokes boundary layer is small compared with a characteristic radius of the pipe and is of order ε 2 when it is large compared with the same radius.

the first-order steady streaming in a pipe of slow varying cross-section is of order unity and is of the same order as the oscillatory velocity in the Stokes layer when the characteristic thickness of this layer is large compared with the radius of curvature of the pipe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the unsteady viscous flow through a pipe of slowly variable cross-section.
the study of the unsteady motion in a pipe of variable cross-section.
a study of the steady streaming generated in an unsteady viscous flow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steady streaming is a net flow towards that end of the pipe which has the larger radius.
the steady streaming is always directed towards the wider end.
the first-order steady streaming in a pipe of varying cross-section can be predicted by a simple model which takes into account the effect of the pipe wall on the Stokes layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first-order steady streaming consists of a net flow towards a region of smaller cross-sectional area.
the steady streaming in a pipe of varying radius consists of a net flow in the direction of the wider end of a pipe.
the first-order steady streaming consists of a net flow towards that end of the pipe at which the mean radius is larger.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the steady streaming generated in pipes of slowly varying cross sections can be very different from the classical steady streaming generated in tubes with uniform cross sections, and the difference depends on the geometry of the tube and the thickness of the Stokes boundary layer.
the geometry of a slowly varying pipe can have a profound effect on the steady streaming induced by an oscillatory pressure gradient.

, in the limit of a slowly varying cross-section, the steady streaming generated by an oscillatory motion in the fluid can have a large magnitude, even when the amplitude of the oscillatory motion is small.
